extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to PLOS journals (researchers preparing data for publication)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, sharing, and describing the data underlying manuscripts submitted to PLOS journals, including what must be in the Data Availability Statement and acceptable sharing methods and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of data required
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS journals require authors to make all data necessary to replicate their study’s findings publicly available without restriction at the time of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specific legal or ethical restrictions prohibit public sharing, authors must indicate how others may obtain access to the data. Publication is conditional on compliance; if restrictions come to light after publication PLOS may post a Correction, Editorial Expression of Concern, contact institutions/funders, or retract the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Availability Statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a manuscript, authors must provide a Data Availability Statement describing compliance with PLOS' data policy. If the article is accepted, the Data Availability Statement will be published as part of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement should list repositories, persistent identifiers, licensing information, or explain restrictions and provide contact details for access where applicable. Placeholder language for accession numbers/DOIs is allowed at submission if these will be provided after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal data set definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must share the “minimal data set” defined as the data required to replicate all study findings reported in the article, as well as related metadata and methods. Authors must comply with field-specific standards for preparation, recording, and deposition of data when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of minimal data: values behind means/SDs and other reported measures, values used to build graphs, points extracted from images for analysis. Authors do not need to submit entire raw datasets if only a portion was used or if field standards call for sharing processed data. PLOS does not permit references to “data not shown.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Image data requirements (sample and original images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to provide sample image data in support of all reported results; for certain journals and submissions (PLOS Biology, PLOS ONE, PLOS Climate, PLOS Water, PLOS Global Public Health or PLOS Mental Health submitted on/after July 1, 2019) original, uncropped and minimally adjusted images supporting all blot and gel results must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original images need not be provided at initial submission but will be required during peer review or before acceptance. PLOS may request underlying image data post-publication to investigate concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit in a public data repository (strongly recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: All data and related metadata underlying reported findings should be deposited in appropriate public data repositories (subject-specific or generalist), unless already provided as part of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If field-specific deposition standards exist, authors must comply (examples: ArrayExpress/GEO for microarray data; GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ for sequences). The Data Availability Statement must list repository name(s) and DOIs, accession numbers, codes, or other persistent identifiers and, where available, licensing information. Additional guidance on acceptable repositories is provided by PLOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS encourages authors to cite any publicly available research data in their reference list; data citations must include a persistent identifier (such as a DOI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations of data sets should include the minimum information recommended by DataCite and follow journal style. PLOS supports the Data Citation roadmap (FORCE11/DCIP). Example citation format is provided in policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Information data: acceptable formats and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Data may be included in Supporting Information files, though depositing to a repository is encouraged. Supporting Information files should be in standard, extractable file formats and each file should be less than 20 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no field standard exists, maximize accessibility and reusability (spreadsheets preferable to PDFs or images for tabulated data). Supporting Information files are uploaded to figshare and are published exactly as provided (not copyedited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plans (DMPs) encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS encourages authors to prepare Data Management Plans before conducting research and to make those plans available to editors, reviewers and readers who wish to assess them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may consult funder/institution resources, the Digital Curation Centre, DMPTool, Data Stewardship Wizard, and other DMP guidance linked by PLOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable access restrictions must be justified and disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS recognizes that legal or ethical frameworks may prevent or limit data release; where these frameworks apply, authors must make these limitations clear in the Data Availability Statement at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not acceptable for an author to be the sole named individual responsible for ensuring data access. Where possible, deposit restricted data in a repository that allows controlled access or direct requests to a non-author institutional point of contact (e.g., data access or ethics committee) to ensure long-term stability and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party data: disclosure and access information required
rubrics_metrics.description: For third-party data that authors cannot legally distribute, the Data Availability Statement must include a description of the data set and the third-party source, verification of permission to use the data set (if applicable), contact information for others to apply for access, and any known restrictions to accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should properly cite and acknowledge the data source. Other researchers should be able to access the dataset in the same manner as the authors unless allowable restrictions apply under PLOS policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human research participant and sensitive data: privacy protections and restricted access
rubrics_metrics.description: For human research participant data and other sensitive data, authors are encouraged to share de-identified/anonymized data; when data cannot be publicly shared, authors may make data available upon request and must explain restrictions and provide an appropriate institutional contact in the Data Availability Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior consult with an ethics committee is recommended. Data sharing must not compromise participant privacy; it is inappropriate to publicly share personally identifiable information (names, initials, addresses, IP addresses, specific dates, contact information, location data). Indirect identifiers that could lead to re-identification should also be considered. Steps to protect privacy may include de-identification, adding noise, blocking database portions, or license agreements directed at privacy concerns. PLOS links to external guidance on de-identification and clinical trial data sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for qualitative data
rubrics_metrics.description: For qualitative research, authors should make excerpts of transcripts relevant to the study available in an appropriate repository, within the paper, or upon request if they cannot be shared publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sharing excerpts would violate participant consent or agreements, authors should explain this restriction and state what data they can share. The Qualitative Data Repository is referenced for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other sensitive data (non-human): consult field guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some non-human data may be sensitive and inappropriate to share publicly (e.g., locations of sensitive archaeological sites, locations of endangered or threatened species, data from protected areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult established field guidelines and all applicable local laws and share data as appropriate after doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable data access restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS journals will not consider manuscripts for which certain factors influence authors’ ability to share data, such as authors refusing to share because of personal interests (patents or potential future publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conclusions depend solely on proprietary data that cannot be shared and others cannot access the data in the same manner, the manuscript must include an analysis of publicly available data that validates the study’s conclusions so that others can reproduce the analysis and build on the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of private reviewer access during peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing private data access to reviewers and editors during the peer review process is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many repositories permit private reviewer access and have policies for public release at publication. When depositing with an integrated repository, authors receive a provisional DOI and a private reviewer URL which can be included in the Data Availability Statement; upon acceptance, publication and public release are coordinated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of placeholder accession numbers at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If accession numbers or DOIs are not available at submission, authors may include placeholder language in the Data Availability Statement indicating these will be provided after acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal office will contact authors before publication to request the accession/DOI and hold the paper until it is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository licensing should not be more restrictive than CC BY
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors use repositories with stated licensing policies, those policies should not be more restrictive than the Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide licensing information in the Data Availability Statement where available. PLOS partner repositories may have submission fees; authors are not obligated to use a specific repository and PLOS does not gain financially from partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for institutional/non-author point of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS discourages naming an author as the sole point of contact for restricted data access; recommend depositing restricted data in a repository that permits controlled access or directing requests to a non-author institutional contact (data access committee, ethics committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A durable institutional contact ensures access even if authors change email, institutions, or become unavailable. Journal contact (plosone@plos.org) is provided for additional help or unusual cases.
